'''Mladen Bestvina''' (born 1959)<ref name="hazu">{{cite web|url=https://www.info.hazu.hr/en/clanovi/mladen-bestvina/|title=Mladen Bestvina|work=info.hazu.hr|publisher=[[Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts]]|language=English|accessdate=2013-03-29}}</ref> is a [[Croatian-American]] [[mathematician]] working in the area of [[geometric group theory]]. He is a Distinguished Professor in the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Utah]].

==Life and career==
Mladen Bestvina is a three-time medalist at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] (two silver medals in 1976 and 1978 and a bronze medal in 1977).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=68 | title=Mladen Bestvina | work=imo-official.org | publisher=[[International Mathematical Olympiad]] | accessdate=2010-02-10}}</ref> He received a B. Sc. in 1982 from the [[University of Zagreb]].<ref>[https://www.math.utah.edu/research/brochure/bestvina2.pdf Research brochure: Mladen Bestvina], Department of Mathematics, [[University of Utah]]. Accessed February 8, 2010</ref> He obtained a PhD in Mathematics in 1984 at the [[University of Tennessee]] under the direction of John Walsh.<ref>[https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=3879 Mladen F. Bestvina],  [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]. Accessed February 8, 2010.</ref>  He was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 1987-88 and again in 1990–91.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars|title=Scholars &#124; Institute for Advanced Study|date=August 14, 2015|website=www.ias.edu}}</ref> Bestvina had been a faculty member at [[UCLA]], and joined the faculty in the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Utah]] in 1993.<ref name="aft">[https://www.math.utah.edu/newsletter/aftermath/2008-04.pdf Mladen Bestvina: Distinguished Professor], ''Aftermath'', vol. 8, no. 4, April 2008. Department of Mathematics, [[University of Utah]].</ref> He was appointed a Distinguished Professor at the [[University of Utah]] in 2008.<ref name="aft"/>
Bestvina received the [[Sloan Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Fellowship]] in 1988–89<ref>[https://www.math.utah.edu/research/sloan.html Sloan Fellows.] Department of Mathematics, [[University of Utah]]. Accessed February 8, 2010</ref><ref>[http://www.sloan.org/fellowships/list/filter/field/lastnamef/letter/B/page/175 Sloan Research Fellowships], {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110424085200/http://www.sloan.org/fellowships/list/filter/field/lastnamef/letter/B/page/175 |date=2011-04-24 }} [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]]. Accessed February 8, 2010</ref> and a [[PECASE|Presidential Young Investigator Award]] in 1988–91.<ref>[https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward.do?AwardNumber=8857452 Award Abstract #8857452. Mathematical Sciences: Presidential Young Investigator.] [[National Science Foundation]]. Accessed February 8, 2010</ref>

Bestvina gave an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited address at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Beijing]] in 2002,<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200111/people.pdf Invited Speakers for ICM2002.] [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 48, no. 11,  December 2001; pp. 1343&nbsp;1345</ref>, was topology section member in Madrid in 2006 <ref>[https://www.mathunion.org/icm/program-committee-and-sectional-panels-2006-madrid-spain Program Committee and Sectional Panels 2006 Madrid, Spain, Sectional Panels Topology]</ref> and gave a plenary lecture at virtual ICM 2022.<ref>[https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Bestvina ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers Mladen Bestvina]</ref>
He also gave a Unni Namboodiri Lecture in Geometry and Topology at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>[http://www.math.uchicago.edu/research/lectures.shtml Annual Lecture Series.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100609213648/http://www.math.uchicago.edu/research/lectures.shtml |date=2010-06-09 }}  Department of Mathematics, [[University of Chicago]]. Accessed February 9, 2010</ref>

Bestvina served as an Editorial Board member for the [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200709/tx070901178p.pdf Officers and Committee Members], [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 54, no. 9, October 2007, pp. 1178&nbsp;1187</ref> and as an associate editor of the [[Annals of Mathematics]].<ref>[http://annals.princeton.edu/annals/about/journal/editorial.html Editorial Board], {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20090519205537/http://annals.princeton.edu/annals/about/journal/editorial.html |date=2009-05-19 }} [[Annals of Mathematics]]. Accessed February 8, 2010</ref> Currently he is an editorial board member for [[Duke Mathematical Journal]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dukeupress.edu/duke-mathematical-journal|title=Duke Mathematical Journal}}</ref> [[Geometric and Functional Analysis]],<ref>[https://www.springer.com/birkhauser/mathematics/journal/39?detailsPage=editorialBoard Editorial Board], [[Geometric and Functional Analysis]]. Accessed February 8, 2010</ref> [[Geometry & Topology|Geometry and Topology]],<ref>[https://msp.org/gt/about/journal/editorial.html Editorial Board] [[Geometry & Topology|Geometry and Topology]]</ref> the ''Journal of Topology and Analysis'',<ref>[http://www.worldscinet.com/jta/mkt/editorial.shtml Editorial Board.] ''Journal of Topology and Analysis''. Accessed February 8, 2010</ref> ''Groups, Geometry and Dynamics'',<ref>[https://www.ems-ph.org/journals/editorial.php?jrn=ggd Editorial Board], ''Groups, Geometry and Dynamics''. Accessed February 8, 2010</ref> ''Michigan Mathematical Journal'',<ref>[http://www.math.lsa.umich.edu/mmj/ Editorial Board], ''Michigan Mathematical Journal''. Accessed February 8, 2010</ref> ''Rocky Mountain Journal of Mathematics'',<ref>[https://rmmc.asu.edu/rmj/editors.html Editorial Board], Rocky Mountain Journal of Mathematics. Accessed February 8, 2010</ref> and ''Glasnik Matematicki''.<ref>[https://www.math.utah.edu/~milicic/Glasnik/index.html Editorial Board], Glasnik Matematicki. Accessed February 8, 2010</ref>

In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref> Since 2012, he has been a correspondent member of the HAZU (Croatian Academy of Science and Art).<ref name="hazu"/>

==Mathematical contributions==
A 1988 monograph of Bestvina<ref>Bestvina, Mladen, ''Characterizing ''k''-dimensional universal Menger compacta''.
[[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 71 (1988), no. 380</ref> gave an abstract topological characterization of universal Menger compacta in all dimensions; previously only the cases of dimension 0 and 1 were well understood. John Walsh wrote in a review of Bestvina's monograph: 'This work, which formed the author's Ph.D. thesis at the [[University of Tennessee]], represents a monumental step forward, having moved the status of the topological structure of higher-dimensional Menger compacta from one of "close to total ignorance" to one of "complete understanding".'<ref>John J. Walsh, Review of: Bestvina, Mladen, ''Characterizing ''k''-dimensional universal Menger compacta''. [[Mathematical Reviews]], MR0920964 (89g:54083), 1989</ref>

In a 1992 paper Bestvina and Feighn obtained a ''Combination Theorem'' for [[word-hyperbolic group]]s.<ref>M. Bestvina and M. Feighn, [http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?verb=Display&version=1.0&service=UI&handle=euclid.jdg/1214447806&page=record A combination theorem for negatively curved groups.] [[Journal of Differential Geometry]], Volume 35 (1992), pp. 85–101</ref> The theorem provides a set of sufficient conditions for [[free product|amalgamated free products]] and [[HNN extension]]s of word-hyperbolic groups to again be word-hyperbolic. The Bestvina–Feighn Combination Theorem became a standard tool in [[geometric group theory]] and has had many applications and generalizations (e.g.<ref>Emina ALibegovic, [http://journals.cambridge.org/action/displayAbstract?fromPage=online&aid=306432 A Combination Theorem for Relatively Hyperbolic Groups.] [[Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society]] vol. 37 (2005),  pp. 459–466</ref><ref>Francois Dahmani,  [http://www.emis.de/journals/GT/ftp/main/2003/2003-27.pdf Combination of convergence groups.] [[Geometry and Topology]], Volume 7 (2003), 933–963</ref><ref>I. Kapovich, [http://www.worldscinet.com/ijac/11/1102/S0218196701000553.html The combination theorem and quasiconvexity.]  International Journal of Algebra and Computation, Volume: 11 (2001), no. 2,  pp. 185–216</ref><ref>M. Mitra, [http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?verb=Display&version=1.0&service=UI&handle=euclid.jdg/1214460609&page=record Cannon–Thurston maps for trees of hyperbolic metric spaces.] [[Journal of Differential Geometry]], Volume 48 (1998), Number 1, 135–164</ref>).

Bestvina and Feighn also gave the first published treatment of [[Eliyahu Rips|Rips']] theory of stable group actions on [[Real tree|'''R'''-trees]] (the [[Rips machine]])<ref>M. Bestvina and M. Feighn. ''Stable actions of groups on real trees.'' [[Inventiones Mathematicae]], vol. 121 (1995), no. 2, pp. 287&nbsp;321</ref> In particular their paper gives a proof of the [[Morgan–Shalen conjecture]]<ref>[[John Morgan (mathematician)|Morgan, John W.]], [[Peter Shalen|Shalen, Peter B.]], ''Free actions of surface groups on R-trees''.
[[Topology (journal)|Topology]], vol. 30 (1991), no. 2, pp. 143–154</ref> that a [[finitely generated group]] ''G'' admits a free isometric [[Group action (mathematics)|action]] on an  [[Real tree|'''R'''-tree]] if and only if ''G'' is a [[free product]] of surface groups, [[free group]]s and [[free abelian group]]s.

A 1992 paper of Bestvina and [[Michael Handel|Handel]] introduced the notion of a [[train track map]] for representing elements of [[Out(Fn)|Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>)]].<ref name="BH92">Mladen Bestvina, and Michael Handel, [https://www.jstor.org/pss/2946562 ''Train tracks and automorphisms of free groups.'']  [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2), vol.  135  (1992),  no. 1, pp. 1–51</ref>   In the same paper they introduced the notion of a ''relative train track'' and applied train track methods to solve<ref name="BH92"/> the ''Scott conjecture'', which says that for every automorphism ''α'' of a finitely generated [[free group]] ''F<sub>n</sub>'' the fixed subgroup of ''α'' is free of [[rank of a group|rank]] at most ''n''.  Since then train tracks became a standard tool in the study of algebraic, geometric and dynamical properties of automorphisms of free groups and of subgroups of Out(''F<sub>n</sub>'').    Examples of applications of train tracks include: a theorem of Brinkmann<ref name="Br">P. Brinkmann, [https://doi.org/10.1007%2FPL00001647 ''Hyperbolic automorphisms of free groups.'']  [[Geometric and Functional Analysis]], vol. 10  (2000),  no. 5, pp. 1071–1089</ref> proving that for an automorphism ''α'' of ''F<sub>n</sub>'' the mapping torus group of ''α'' is [[word-hyperbolic group|word-hyperbolic]] if and only if ''α'' has no periodic conjugacy classes; a theorem of Bridson and Groves<ref name="BG">Martin R. Bridson and Daniel Groves. [https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/~bridson/papers/BG1/ ''The quadratic isoperimetric inequality for mapping tori of free-group automorphisms.''] Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society, to appear.</ref> that for every automorphism ''α'' of ''F<sub>n</sub>'' the mapping torus group of ''α'' satisfies a quadratic [[Dehn function|isoperimetric inequality]]; a proof of algorithmic solvability of the [[conjugacy problem]] for free-by-cyclic groups;<ref name="BMMV">O. Bogopolski, A. Martino, O. Maslakova, E. Ventura, [http://journals.cambridge.org/action/displayAbstract?fromPage=online&aid=471663 ''The conjugacy problem is solvable in free-by-cyclic groups.'']  [[Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society]], vol. 38  (2006),  no. 5, pp. 787–794</ref> and others.

Bestvina, Feighn and Handel later proved that the group Out(''F<sub>n</sub>'') satisfies the [[Tits alternative]],<ref name="BFH00">Mladen Bestvina, Mark Feighn, and Michael Handel. [http://www.emis.de/journals/Annals/151_2/bestvina.pdf ''The Tits alternative for Out(F<sub>n</sub>). I. Dynamics of exponentially-growing automorphisms.''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606014154/http://www.emis.de/journals/Annals/151_2/bestvina.pdf |date=2011-06-06 }}  [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2), vol. 151  (2000),  no. 2, pp. 517–623</ref><ref name="BFH05">Mladen Bestvina, Mark Feighn, and Michael Handel.  [http://annals.princeton.edu/annals/2005/161-1/p01.xhtml ''The Tits alternative for Out(F<sub>n</sub>). II. A Kolchin type theorem.'']  [[Annals of Mathematics]] (2), vol. 161  (2005),  no. 1, pp. 1–59</ref> settling a long-standing open problem.

In a 1997 paper<ref>Bestvina, Mladen and Brady, Noel, ''Morse theory and finiteness properties of groups''.  [[Inventiones Mathematicae]], vol. 129 (1997), no. 3, pp. 445–470</ref> Bestvina and Brady developed a version of [[discrete Morse theory]] for cubical complexes and applied it to study homological finiteness properties of subgroups of right-angled [[Artin group]]s. In particular, they constructed an example of a group which provides a counter-example to either the [[Whitehead conjecture|Whitehead asphericity conjecture]] or to the [[Eilenberg−Ganea conjecture]], thus showing that at least one of these conjectures must be false. Brady subsequently used their Morse theory technique to construct the first example of a [[finitely presented group|finitely presented]] subgroup of a [[word-hyperbolic group]] that is not itself word-hyperbolic.<ref>Brady, Noel,  ''Branched coverings of cubical complexes and subgroups of hyperbolic groups''. [[Journal of the London Mathematical Society]] (2), vol. 60 (1999), no. 2, pp. 461–480</ref>
